title: 271. Functions, Graphs & Transformations: Graphing a Shifted Square Root Function
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Domain of a Shifted Square Root Function
questions.learningObjective: Determine the domain of a square root function after a horizontal shift.
questions.question: What is the domain of \(y=\sqrt{x-3}\)?
questions.explanation: The radicand must be nonnegative. Set \(x-3\ge 0\), so \(x\ge 3\). Therefore the domain is \(x\ge 3\), and option A is correct.
questions.hint: The expression inside a square root must be greater than or equal to zero.

questions.concept: Range of a Shifted Square Root Function
questions.learningObjective: Determine the range of a square root function after a vertical shift.
questions.question: What is the range of \(y=\sqrt{x+2}+1\)?
questions.explanation: The square root \(\sqrt{x+2}\) is always nonnegative, so its smallest value is \(0\). Adding \(1\) gives a smallest value of \(1\). Therefore the range is \(y\ge 1\), and option B is correct.
questions.hint: Start with the range of the parent square root function and apply the vertical shift.

questions.concept: Starting Point of a Shifted Square Root Graph
questions.learningObjective: Identify the starting point of a shifted square root graph.
questions.question: What is the starting point of the graph of \(y=\sqrt{x-4}+2\)?
questions.explanation: The graph of \(y=\sqrt{x-h}+k\) starts at \((h,k)\). Here \(h=4\) and \(k=2\), so the starting point is \((4,2)\). Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: The starting point is the point where the radicand equals zero.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the graph that matches a given square root equation.
questions.question: Which description matches the graph of \(y=\sqrt{x+1}-3\)?

options.label: A
options.text: The graph of \(y=\sqrt{x}\) shifted right \(1\) unit and down \(3\) units

options.label: B
options.text: The graph of \(y=\sqrt{x}\) shifted left \(1\) unit and down \(3\) units

questions.explanation: The expression \(x+1\) can be written as \(x-(-1)\), so the horizontal shift is left \(1\) unit. The \(-3\) outside the square root indicates a vertical shift down \(3\) units. Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: Inside the square root, \(x-h\) gives a shift of \(h\) units to the right.

questions.concept: Writing a Shifted Square Root Equation
questions.learningObjective: Write the equation of a shifted square root function from its starting point.
questions.question: A square root graph has starting point \((2,-5)\). Which equation could represent the graph?
questions.explanation: A square root graph with starting point \((h,k)\) has equation \(y=\sqrt{x-h}+k\). For \((2,-5)\), we need \(h=2\) and \(k=-5\), so the equation is \(y=\sqrt{x-2}-5\). Therefore option B is correct.

questions.concept: Horizontal Shift of a Square Root Function
questions.learningObjective: Determine the horizontal shift from the equation of a square root function.
questions.question: How is the graph of \(y=\sqrt{x}\) shifted to obtain the graph of \(y=\sqrt{x-5}\)?
questions.explanation: The equation \(y=\sqrt{x-5}\) is in the form \(y=\sqrt{x-h}\) with \(h=5\). A positive \(h\) shifts the graph of \(y=\sqrt{x}\) to the right by \(5\) units. Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: In \(y=\sqrt{x-h}\), the graph shifts \(h\) units horizontally.

questions.concept: Domain of a Shifted Square Root Function with a Coefficient
questions.learningObjective: Determine the domain of a square root function with a linear radicand.
questions.question: What is the domain of \(y=\sqrt{2x-6}+1\)?
questions.explanation: The radicand must be nonnegative: \(2x-6\ge 0\). Add \(6\): \(2x\ge 6\). Divide by \(2\): \(x\ge 3\). Therefore the domain is \(x\ge 3\), and option B is correct.
questions.hint: Solve the inequality obtained by setting the radicand greater than or equal to zero.

questions.concept: Range of a Reflected and Shifted Square Root Function
questions.learningObjective: Determine the range of a square root function with a negative coefficient and vertical shift.
questions.question: What is the range of \(y=-\sqrt{x-1}+4\)?
questions.explanation: The expression \(-\sqrt{x-1}\) is always nonpositive, so its largest value is \(0\). Adding \(4\) gives a largest value of \(4\). Therefore the range is \(y\le 4\), and option B is correct.
questions.hint: A negative sign in front of the square root reflects the graph downward.

questions.concept: Identifying a Shifted Square Root Function from Domain and Range
questions.learningObjective: Determine the square root function that has a given domain and range.
questions.question: Which function has domain \(x\ge -3\) and range \(y\ge 2\)?
questions.explanation: The domain \(x\ge -3\) comes from \(x+3\ge 0\), so the radicand is \(x+3\). The range \(y\ge 2\) comes from adding \(2\) outside the square root. Therefore the function is \(y=\sqrt{x+3}+2\), and option A is correct.
questions.hint: The domain determines the expression inside the square root, and the range determines the vertical shift.

questions.concept: Describing a Shifted Square Root Graph
questions.learningObjective: Describe the horizontal and vertical shifts of a square root function.
questions.question: How is the graph of \(y=\sqrt{x}\) shifted to obtain the graph of \(y=\sqrt{x+4}-1\)?
questions.explanation: The expression \(x+4\) can be written as \(x-(-4)\), so the horizontal shift is left \(4\) units. The \(-1\) outside the square root indicates a vertical shift down \(1\) unit. Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: Rewrite \(x+4\) as \(x-(-4)\) to determine the horizontal shift.
